newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks end slightly down on correction.
newsitem.headline: China stocks end slightly down on correction.

text.p: China's A and B shares closed slightly lower on Tuesday on a correction but brokers said they expected bullish sentiment to lift prices before next month's lunar new year.
Shanghai's foreign currency B share index inched down 0.471 points, or 0.72 percent, to 65.401 and Shenzhen's B index fell just 0.10 points, or 0.18 percent, to 153.17.
Brokers said investor confidence in the economy, boosted recently by forecasts that included a prediction of six percent inflation this year, could fuel a rebound this week.
"Generally speaking, today's fall is just a technical correction, which will support the index to move up further in the next few days," one Shanghai broker said.
On the Shanghai B market, Shanghai Industrial Sewing Machine was the biggest loser on expectations of poor 1996 results, slipping $0.010, or 5.68 percent, to $0.166 on volume of 41,900 shares.
Shanghai Narcissus Electric Appliances was the most active share on institutional selling, but it ended flat at $0.184 amid speculative buying late in the session.
On Shenzhen's B share market, Dadonghai Tourism was the poorest performing stock, sinking HK$0.15, or 3.61 percent, on profit-taking to HK$4.00 on volume of 3.86 million shares.
Changan Automobile was the second-biggest loser, falling HK$0.15 to HK$4.65 on trade of two million shares.
The domestic A share markets in both Shanghai and Shenzhen also fell on a correction, brokers said.
Shanghai's A share index was down 2.73 points, or 0.27 percent, to 997.96 on volume of 295.7 million shares worth 2.8 billion yuan.
Shanxi Fenjiu was the biggest loser, falling 0.22 yuan, or 2.95 percent, to 7.23 yuan on volume of 2.3 million shares.
Shenzhen's A share index lost 0.67 points, or 0.18 percent, to 370.14 with turnover falling to 6.2 billion yuan from Monday's 7.37 billion yuan.
Department store owner Tongcheng fell 0.34 yuan, or 3.02 percent, to 13.79 yuan on turnover of 1.64 million shares.
